newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL- More Swedes, 30 pct, in favour of EMU.
newsitem.headline: POLL- More Swedes, 30 pct, in favour of EMU.

text.p: Swedes are becoming more positive about their country joining Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) with one in three now supporting participation, a poll in Dagens Industri said on Friday.
About one year ago only one in four Swedes was in favour of the project, the survey by pollster Gallup in the business daily showed.
The number of those against EMU has fallen to about half of the population from about 60 percent in March 1996, it found.

"Support for joining EMU will increase the closer we get to the start of the project," the newspaper quoted Lars Calmfors, head of a separate official commission examining EMU for the government, as saying.
"I believe a majority of Swedes will take a positive position to joining EMU at a later date," Calmfors told the newspaper.
The question that was put to 1,000 Swedes between June 28 and July 2 for the poll was "Are you for or against Sweden participating in a common currency within the European Union?"

Swedes opted to stay out of EMU from the project's planned 1999 start but left the door open to joining at a later date. The government cited low public support as the main reason for staying out of EMU for the time being.
